resources.string: Simulated controller with live data. Nothing is sent to hardware.
Turn it on to find controllers with a BLE module.
Android needs this permission before FOCTuner can scan for Bluetooth controllers. It isn\'t used for anything else.
Android 11 and older only allow Bluetooth scans with location access. FOCTuner never reads your location.
This device has no Bluetooth LE.
Is the controller powered and its BLE module lit?
Is the app port set to UART (App settings › General)?
Is another phone or laptop already connected to it?
Plug the controller in with a USB‑C or OTG cable. Android asks to allow access the first time.
Nothing announced on this network. Controllers with WiFi announce themselves; others need an address.
No reply from %1$s. Check that it is powered and in range.
Settings have not been read yet.
Kept in the app only, not stored on the controller
Firmware %1$s stores its settings in a different layout than the %2$s definitions in this app. Reading and writing settings is blocked so nothing gets corrupted.
The controller didn\'t answer. Check the connection and read again.
%1$s is outside its allowed range. Fix it before writing.
The motor stays off until the kill switch input is released.
Firmware terminal. Send help to list the commands this firmware supports.
No reply. The firmware ignores a command while the previous one is still running.
Live data, terminal and settings go to the selected controller.
Only this controller answered. Others on the bus need a unique controller ID and the same CAN baud rate.
The firmware reported a fault this version of FOCTuner doesn\'t know. Update the app, or look the code up in the firmware\'s datatypes.h.
Usually regenerative braking on a full battery. Brake more gently when charged, or lower the battery regen current limit.
The battery is nearly empty, or it sagged under load. Check the charge level, the BMS and the battery wiring.
The MOSFET driver reported a problem, often a shorted MOSFET or phase wire. Check the motor wires before driving again.
Motor current spiked past the absolute maximum and the output was cut. Common causes: wrong motor parameters, a loose phase wire, or limits too close to the hardware maximum.
The MOSFETs reached their temperature cutoff, so output was reduced or stopped. Let it cool, and check airflow and how the controller is mounted.
The motor temperature sensor reached its cutoff. Let it cool. If it trips quickly, check the sensor type in motor settings.
The gate driver supply voltage is above its limit. This points to a hardware problem on the controller.
The gate driver supply dropped too low, often from heavy battery sag or a failing regulator on the board.
The processor\'s 3.3 V supply dipped. Check for accessories drawing too much from the 3.3 V or 5 V pins.
The firmware stopped responding and the watchdog restarted it. Note what you were doing, and update the firmware if a newer version exists.
The SPI encoder isn\'t answering. Check its cable and connector.
The sin/cos encoder amplitude is below its minimum. Check the wiring and the gap between sensor and magnet.
The sin/cos encoder amplitude is above its maximum. Check the wiring and the encoder gain settings.
The firmware in flash failed its checksum. Reflash the firmware before riding.
The sensor reads well away from zero with no current flowing. Make sure the motor is still when the controller powers up. If it persists, the sensor may be damaged.
The three phase currents don\'t add up to zero. Check for a loose or damaged phase wire or connector.
The hardware protection switched the MOSFETs off instantly, typically from a short or a severe current spike. Inspect the motor and phase wires.
The resolver interface lost track of the rotor position. Check the resolver wiring.
The resolver signal is out of range. Check the wiring and its shielding.
There is no signal from the resolver. Check that it is connected.
The stored app configuration failed its checksum. Write the app configuration again, from a backup if you have one.
The stored motor configuration failed its checksum. Write the motor configuration again, from a backup if you have one.
Check that the magnet is in place and centered over the sensor.
The magnetic field at the sensor is too strong. Increase the gap between magnet and sensor.
The phase voltage filters gave implausible readings. Run motor detection again; if it persists, the board may be damaged.
The encoder reported an internal error. Check its wiring and supply.
The accessory supply output is shorted or overloaded. Disconnect lights and other accessories and check their wiring.
The encoder position stopped matching the motor. The magnet may have moved on the shaft, or the encoder mount is loose.
The motor turned faster than the configured ERPM limit.
The motor turned slower than the configured minimum ERPM.
The motor spun past the absolute maximum ERPM and the output was cut. Check the speed limits in motor settings.
